Using the Arrhenius equation in logarithmic form:
$$\log \frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$$

Given data:
* $k_1 = 5000\text{ sec}^{-1}$ at $T_1 = 25\text{ }^{\circ}\text{C} = 298\text{ K}$
* $k_2 = 10000\text{ sec}^{-1}$
* $E_a = 6 \times 10^4\text{ J mol}^{-1}$
* $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

Substitute the values:
$$\log \left( \frac{10000}{5000} \right) = \frac{60000}{2.303 \times 8.314} \left( \frac{T_2 - 298}{298 T_2} \right)$$
$$\log(2) = 3133.63 \left( \frac{T_2 - 298}{298 T_2} \right)$$
$$0.3010 = 3133.63 \left( \frac{T_2 - 298}{298 T_2} \right)$$

Solving for $T_2$:
$$T_2 \approx 307.2\text{ K} \text{ (or } 34.2\text{ }^{\circ}\text{C)}$$
proTip: Always convert Celsius temperatures to Kelvin before substituting into the Arrhenius equation.
